title: kv-cache: improve memory management & eviction heuristics for fragmentation, paging, and spillover
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: The KV cache has been a primary source of memory fragmentation and unexpected OOMs under mixed workload patterns (short chat sessions interleaved with long completion requests). This PR implements a set of coordinated changes to reduce fragmentation, enable paging/spillover to host memory with controlled performance degradation, and adjust eviction heuristics to prioritize low-cost defragmentation and hot-prefix retention. Goals:
- Reduce in-GPU fragmentation and peak resident set size under mixed workloads
- Provide predictable spillover behavior to host memory when GPU memory is constrained
- Improve scheduler/batcher awareness of KV cache pressure to avoid pathological batching that exacerbates fragmentation
- Keep tail latency regressions <5% and improve throughput where possible

What changed (summary):
- Introduced a compacting defragmentation pass in pkg/serving/kv_cache/defrag.go that runs opportunistically when fragmentation ratio exceeds a threshold. The pass uses page-aligned moves and updates KV pointers atomically to avoid stalls.
- Added a paged allocator in pkg/serving/kv_cache/page_allocator.go which divides KV allocations into fixed-size pages (default 256KB) and supports spill-to-host for cold pages. Spill is asynchronous with an LRU-ish ranking that prefers spilling large sparse pages first.
- New eviction heuristics in pkg/serving/evict/heuristics.go: cost-based scoring combining last-access, page-density, and expected recompute cost; prefers evicting pages that free contiguous ranges to aid defrag.
- Scheduler/batcher integration in pkg/serving/scheduler/batcher.go: the batcher now exposes a KV-pressure hint (low/medium/high) and rejects or downsamples batch growth if pressure is high. This prevents large batches from increasing KV fragmentation during peak allocation churn.
- Telemetry and metrics: added kv_cache.fragmentation_ratio, kv_cache.paged_bytes, kv_cache.spilled_pages, kv_cache.defrag_runs, and eviction.score_distribution to docs/metrics/kv-cache.md and production dashboards.
- Tests + benchmarks: added test/perf/kv_cache_eviction_bench.go and unit tests that simulate mixed short/long workloads and assert memory stability over long runs.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit & integration tests
- [x] Perf benchmarks (local and CI)
- [x] Metrics and dashboards updated
- [x] Documentation update (kv-cache.md)

Benchmarks (high level):
- Mixed short/long workload: peak GPU RSS reduced by ~28% on average across runs (N=10), 95th percentile latency +3.4% (within target).
- Cold-start heavy paging stress: throughput drops gracefully; spill-to-host increased token cost ~12% but prevented OOMs seen previously.

Risks & mitigation:
- Defrag pause: defrag runs are incremental and capped to 50ms per run by default; this value is configurable and we added guardrails in the scheduler to avoid doing defrag during tight latency SLO windows.
- Spill throughput variability: documented in release notes and observable via kv_cache.paged_bytes and kv_cache.spill_latency metrics.

Release notes: "Improved KV cache memory management: reduced fragmentation, added paging/spillover support, and smarter eviction heuristics to improve memory stability under mixed workloads. Config knobs exposed for defrag aggressiveness and page size."

release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: reduced fragmentation, added paging/spillover support, smarter eviction heuristics, and batcher integration to avoid fragmentation under high churn. Exposes knobs for defrag aggressiveness and page size. See docs/kv-cache.md for details.
